wa_squish_baby.notes: Access HELD (none added): Baby Squish Rock sits on or near the line between the Palouse to Cascades State Park Trail strip and Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie NF. The catalog's area point (47.43714,-121.66508) falls 36 m OUTSIDE the trail strip on the WA State Parks boundary layer and inside MBS NF on the DNR public-lands and USFS ownership layers; Mountain Project's point (47.43734,-121.6643, a lead only) falls 13 m INSIDE the trail strip. The two points are ~63 m apart and no USGS/OSM feature fixes the rock, so the manager cannot be placed. Owner decision, or a field GPS fix of the rock, needed. The Discover Pass rule would hold either way only if parking is at a State Parks lot, which no official page states for this rock. FA 'Leland Windham & Lauri jae Sweetland (2007)' is on Mountain Project only; not set (FA never from MP alone). The rock is not in the Exit 38 guidebook's Substation section on Rakkup, and no second publisher lists these routes, so grade/length/bolts/anchor rest on MP alone (locked-1src after apply). Area-pin note: the catalog's Baby Squish Rock point is ~63 m from MP's; the USGS 3DEP elevation there reads 1,732 ft vs 1,577 ft at MP's point (MP states 1,856 ft), so the area pin is unreliable; not changed.

wa_substation_glob_job_extension.notes: CATALOG DEFECT: Glob Job Extension is not a standalone route. Mountain Project describes a two-bolt, 15 ft extension that starts at the anchor shared by Glob Job (wa_glob_job) and Glom Don (wa_glom_don) and ends at Rug Monkey's (wa_rug_monkey) anchor; Subversive can also finish into it. The Exit 38 guidebook's Substation list on Rakkup has no such route. Owner call whether it stays its own row or becomes a variation/second pitch of Glob Job. Per the rules only access is proposed; not proposed: bolts null->2 (MP: two-bolt extension), fa stays null (MP: unknown), permit (siblings carry 'No climbing permit. A Discover Pass is needed to park at Olallie State Park.'). pitches 1 left as is. Land-manager nuance for the owner: on the State Parks layer the crag lies in the Palouse to Cascades State Park Trail unit, not the Olallie unit (Olallie polygon ~215 m away); the copied text says 'Olallie State Park' because State Parks' own pages place Deception Crags at Olallie and the verified Deception Wall siblings (also inside the trail strip) say so. The USFS ownership layer is split at this spot (OSM point 10 m inside FS land, area point 13 m inside NON-FS), so the State Parks layer, which is the managing agency's own, decides. In passing: all 19 other Substation rows store pitches 0 and no access.
